tower-of-hanoi.title: Move largest disk first if not on target
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the largest disk that still needs to be placed is not already on its goal peg, first clear any disks above it and move it directly to its goal peg before handling any smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the current configuration has the largest remaining disk on a peg other than its target and it has no smaller disks on top.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Proceeding with moves of smaller disks while the largest disk stays blocked, which later forces an illegal placement of a larger disk onto a smaller one.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursively solve subproblem after moving largest disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After placing the largest needed disk on its goal peg, treat the remaining n‑1 disks as a fresh Tower of Hanoi problem with the same goal pegs, ignoring the already‑placed largest disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Immediately after the largest disk has been moved to its final position.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Continuing to move smaller disks without resetting the sub‑problem, which ends up undoing the placement of the largest disk.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive move sequence for k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Use the classic recursive pattern: move k‑1 disks from the source peg to the auxiliary peg, move the kth (largest) disk to the target peg, then move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary peg onto the target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to transfer a stack of k ordered disks between two pegs while respecting the size rule.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to place a larger disk onto a smaller one directly, breaking the recursive ordering of moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Place move list as final parseable output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the very last list of brackets in the response is the complete move list; any text after it will be ignored by the verifier.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the end of the answer, after all reasoning, output only the move list and nothing else.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending a concluding sentence after the move list, causing the parser to read an empty list as the final answer.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After writing the move list, mentally replay each move from the initial state to confirm that the final peg arrangement exactly matches the goal configuration.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before submitting the answer, run a quick mental simulation of the entire sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves a disk on the wrong peg because the final state was never checked.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Concise final move list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Keep the answer short by placing only the move list as the final element; avoid extra explanations or stray brackets that could be parsed as additional lists.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing the final answer, after any reasoning, output just the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including a partial list of moves earlier in the response, causing the verifier to pick that incomplete list as the solution.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate each move's legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, check that the disk being moved is the topmost disk on its source peg and that the destination peg is empty or has a larger top disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During construction of the move list, after each candidate move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 2 while disk 1 is still on top of the same peg, which is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative smallest-disk cyclic algorithm
tower-of-hanoi.principle: For any Tower of Hanoi instance, repeatedly move the smallest disk to the next peg in a fixed direction (clockwise or counter‑clockwise), and then make the only other legal move; this generates a correct solution.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a systematic way to generate a complete move sequence without recursion, especially for the classic case but also adaptable to arbitrary starts.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Skipping the cyclic move of the smallest disk, leading to a dead‑lock where no legal move exists.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never place a larger disk onto a peg that currently holds any smaller disk; first move those smaller disks elsewhere.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you are about to move a disk onto a peg that is not empty.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 4 onto a peg that already contains disk 3, which is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model finishes its reasoning without outputting the required list of moves, often because it assumes the explanation is sufficient.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always conclude the response with a complete move list, even if the reasoning is long.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens or stops early, leaving the move list unfinished.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the move list ends with a closing bracket and includes all necessary moves before ending the answer.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model adds a move without consulting the current stack state, forgetting that only the top disk can be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, verify that the chosen disk is currently the topmost on its source peg.
